what: The first runs of the compute_uwshcu_inv TorchScript model on the GPU inside the image (four A100 nodes x 128 ranks, the validated layout) failed three times over, each fault behind the previous one; the CPU path of the same image and layout passed (records pi_cam_pausable_g33-*-4x128, g34-nothing-armed-4x128).
native_image: build/pi_cam_promoted_p34 (FTorch on torch 2.14.0+cu126, commit ddff0d18); p35 = p34 with the wheel's CUDA libraries on the rpath (commit 556c0fb1)
model: compute_uwshcu_inv, h256, compact subset, bound in shadow (bit-for-bit) and live, --model-device cuda
outcome: device_count_zero: at the bind (first shallow-convection step) FTorch exited 384 ranks with 'invalid device index N for device count 0' -- the 128 ranks of each of the three nodes other than the job's head node, never the head node's.  Cause (found with the 512-rank bind probe inside 7545429): mpiexec hands every rank the job shell's environment, and PBS had set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES there to the HEAD node's GPU UUIDs; on the other nodes those UUIDs match no device (cudaGetDeviceCount status 100, no CUDA-capable device is detected).  One-node probes could not show it: their only node is the head node.  The Python-side device count before the bind (23ee6c2c, 627ff629) names this now instead of letting FTorch exit; it does not repair it.

nvrtc_builtins: the first forward on the device failed on every rank of a node: TorchScript's fuser compiles with NVRTC, libftorch's runpath resolved the CUDA 12.9 toolkit's libnvrtc.so.12, and that copy wants libnvrtc-builtins.so.12.9, which no run can see; the wheel's NVRTC is 12.6 with its builtins beside it.  Fixed in the build tools (556c0fb1): FTorch's install rpath and the image rpath list the wheel's nvidia/<component>/lib directories ahead of the toolkit; image p35.

cuda_out_of_memory: with the wheel's NVRTC on the library path (p34), 72 and 76 ranks reported 'CUDA error: out of memory' at the first forward: 32 ranks share one 40 GB A100 and each carries its own CUDA context, libtorch's kernels and cuBLAS workspaces.  Nothing else was wrong: no device error, no NVRTC error, no traceback.

mps_one_server_a_node: with mps=1 (one MPS server a node serving the four GPUs, exclusive-process mode) exactly 48 of the head node's 128 ranks bound and the rest got 'CUDA-capable device(s) is/are busy or unavailable': an MPS server serves at most 48 client contexts, and one server was serving all four GPUs.  A user-started daemon in default compute mode works the same way on one node (probe 7545287).

mps_one_server_a_gpu: with one user MPS daemon a GPU on every node, a client naming its GPU by index k>0 found no device (an MPS client's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is read against its server's devices, one); naming index 0 and choosing the server by pipe directory reached every device, and then 409 of 512 ranks hit CUDA out of memory: an MPS client costs about 2.3 GB of the device (probe 7546067: 8 clients a GPU use 18.8 GB, lazy module loading or not), so 32 a GPU cannot use MPS at all.

one_context_a_rank: without MPS, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES unset for mpiexec and set per rank to the node-local GPU index, CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, all 512 ranks bound and ran: shadow bit-for-bit (pi_cam_pausable_g35-uwshcu-sub-shadow-gpu-4x128-repo3), live with the CPU model's health signature (pi_cam_pausable_g35-uwshcu-sub-live-gpu-4x128-repo3).
diagnosis: Node-level facts, none of them the model's: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES must be set per node and per rank (unset before mpiexec, then the node-local rank's GPU index); the site's mps=1 is one server a node and a server serves at most 48 clients; a per-GPU MPS client costs about 2.3 GB of the device, so at 32 ranks a GPU MPS does not fit; one CUDA context a rank fits a 40 GB A100 32 times over with lazy module loading and a 32 MB cuBLAS workspace.
disposition: validation/jobs/pi_cam_pausable_{50step,1month}.pbs launch the CUDA path with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES unset for mpiexec and validation/jobs/gpu_rank_env.sh a rank (one context a rank by default; PYCAM_GPU_MPS=1 starts one MPS server a GPU through validation/jobs/gpu_mps_per_gpu.sh for layouts with few ranks a GPU).  The passing gates are 7546109 (shadow) and 7546110 (live) on image p35; the nothing-armed p35 gate 7544284 passed without any of this.  The one-rank-a-GPU alternative (64 ranks a node) is the layout that fails at initialisation (pi_cam_pausable_gpu-nodes-8x64_50step_failure.json).
